exposure: measures of heat intensity (average degrees over threshold)
cohort: The study included 615,329 preterm and 1,005,576 early-term singleton case-control pairs from national vital records in 50 US metropolitan areas between 1982 and 1988.
finding: Exposure to heatwaves in the week before delivery was consistently associated with increased odds of early-term birth across most definitions, with higher odds for more intense or prolonged heat, but generally showed null associations with preterm birth.
gest_age: Preterm (< 37 weeks), early-term (37-38 weeks), and controls (at least 37 weeks or 39 weeks) singleton births.
